newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand staged a late recovery on the back of a spate of exporter orders to finish one cent up against the dollar from Friday's close.
But bonds took a beating, shedding 10 basis points as U.S. Treasuries fell further on stronger-than-expected November housing starts.
Trade in both markets was quiet, after Monday's public holiday, and dealers said they expected the debt and forex markets to remain thinly traded for the rest of the week.
"I would see our markets remaining pretty subdued going into Christmas, unless we get another big surprise out of the U.S. markets," said one bond dealer.
The rand, which fell sharply last week, slipped again in morning dealings following dollar demand from one big importer. But the currency had regained its composure by the 1400 GMT local close.
"We saw quite a few exporters coming in which helped the rand pull back," said one forex dealer at a major bank.
There was talk of central bank intervention after the rand touched a day's low of 4.7350/7400 but some dealers were sceptical saying there was no need for intervention in such a quiet market.
The rand was last trading at 4.7180/7230, against Friday's 4.7290/7340 close, just off the day's best 4.7140/7190.
Dealers said the currency remained edgy after last week's mauling but most expected it to hold under 4.75. The rand hit an all-time low of 4.7670 bid on October 31.
Against the crosses, the rand was last trading at 7.8693/8824 against sterling from Friday's 7.8485/8582. On the mark it was at 0.3274/3278 from 0.3260/3263.

Bonds had a disappointing day, hit by weaker U.S. Treasuries and also overshadowed by a continuing squeeze at the short end of the yield curve which has lifted three-month BA rates to their highest levels this year.
"We've seen very little local institutional interest and there seems to be some foreign selling," said one bond trader.

Major banks quoted three-month NCD rates steady at high levels of between 17.40 and 17.75 percent after rising continuously towards the end of last week. The 90-day BA rate was also steady at last Friday's high at 16.70 to 17.00 percent.

The Reserve Bank indicated the money market shortage - the amount of money the central band lends to commercial banks for their day-to-day operations - at 9.475 billion rand on Saturday from 9.499 billion rand on Friday.

Money market traders said the liquidity squeeze reflected normal pre-Christmas pressures as annual bonuses were paid out, consumers drew large amounts of money and notes and coins in circulation in the money market system increased.
But the situation had been exacerbated by the continuing problems of the rand, which have deterred foreign investment in South Africa.
Bond Exchange statistics showed foreigners were net buyers of 192.52 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Friday after selling 198.05 million on Thursday.
Nominal cumulative turnover was 3.27 billion rand on Friday after 33.09 billion on Thursday, a settleement day.
